cards.explanation: The answer is silver, friends. Joseph tells his steward to put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack, along with all the food they can carry. Pharaoh had put Joseph over the land of Egypt (Genesis 41:41), and this isn't the first time he has had silver slipped back into their sacks (Genesis 42:25). He's making a habit of it.

The answer is Joseph's silver cup, friends. Joseph says, "Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack…" It goes in along with the silver for Benjamin's grain. Benjamin is the youngest brother, and he has no idea he's carrying a cup that belongs to the ruler of Egypt. Quietest delivery in the whole story.

The answer is "Why have you repaid good with evil?" Joseph tells the steward to ask it (Genesis 44:4). The steward is to say it as soon as he overtakes them, and then he adds the part about the cup. That's a loaded line to get from a man who just caught up with you on the road.

The answer is False, friends. The brothers deny it flat out. They say, "Your servants could not possibly do such a thing." They have no idea the cup is in Benjamin's sack. Imagine being accused of stealing and having nothing to hide but a heavy feeling in your stomach.

The answer is that they brought back the silver they found. That's their argument, friends. They say, "We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found in the mouths of our sacks." Then they ask why they'd steal silver or gold from the house of the steward's master. They figure men who return money they could have kept aren't cup thieves.

The answer is False, friends. The steward trims the deal way down. The brothers said whoever has the cup dies and the rest become slaves. He answers, "As you say…" then adds, "But only the one who is found with the cup will be my slave, and the rest of you shall be free of blame." That's a much lighter sentence than the one they offered themselves.

The answer is oldest, friends. The steward searches, "…beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest…" That means Benjamin's sack is the last one searched. I bet that felt like a very long search for the brothers.

The answer is True, friends. After the cup is found, the brothers all tear their clothes, load their donkeys, and go back to the city. I think the torn clothes show how hard the news hit them. They had already set out for home, and now they turn around.

The answer is that God has exposed the brothers' guilt, friends. Judah, one of the brothers, says, "God has exposed the iniquity of your servants." He doesn't argue or fight the charge. He just puts it plainly and says they are now Joseph's slaves.

The answer is all the brothers along with Benjamin, friends. Judah puts everyone in it. He says, "We are now my lord’s slaves…" and he names "…both we and the one who was found with the cup." That means the brothers and Benjamin together. It's a lot of loyalty to put in one sentence.

The answer is dead, friends. That's what they told Joseph back then, and now Judah repeats it, saying they answered, "The boy’s brother is dead." The brother they mean is Joseph, since Genesis 42:4 calls Benjamin Joseph's brother. And Joseph is the one standing right there listening, while they don't recognize him (Genesis 42:8). I think that's a lot to carry in one sentence.

The answer is True, friends. Judah reports that they told Joseph, "The boy cannot leave his father. If he were to leave, his father would die." That's what they told him back when Joseph asked to see the boy. Now Judah is bringing it up again.

The answer is False, friends. The brothers pushed back. They told their father, "We cannot go down there unless our younger brother goes with us." And then, "So if our younger brother is not with us, we cannot see the man." No Benjamin, no meeting.

The answer is that he'd been torn to pieces, friends. Jacob, the father of these brothers, said, "Surely he has been torn to pieces." He adds that he hasn't seen that son since. I think this one hurts, and Jacob is still carrying it.

The answer is that it would send him to his grave in sorrow, friends. Jacob says that if they take Benjamin and harm comes to him, "…you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow." Sheol is the grave, the place of the dead. He's telling them how heavy a second loss would be.

The answer is that he guaranteed the boy's safety, friends. Judah says, "…your servant guaranteed the boy’s safety to my father…" He told his father he would bear the guilt all his life if he didn't return the boy. So when he asks to stay, he's offering himself in Benjamin's place.

The answer is that Judah begs Joseph to keep him as a slave in place of the boy, friends. Judah says, "Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy. Let him return with his brothers." He offers himself so Benjamin can go home. I think that's a real turn from the Judah who once suggested selling Joseph (Genesis 37:26-27).

The answer is misery, friends. Judah says, "I could not bear to see the misery that would overwhelm him." He's talking about his father if the boy isn't with them. That's why he asks Joseph to keep him instead (Genesis 44:33).
